title: Modes of Convergence for Random Variables

items.title: Almost-sure convergence of real random variables
The almost-sure convergence event is measurable
items.strategy: Rewrite pointwise convergence as a countable intersection over positive rational tolerances, then a union over eventual indices; coordinate-difference measurability gives the claim.

items.title: Convergence in probability
L^p convergence for random variables
Convergence in distribution for real random variables
Limits in probability are unique almost surely
items.strategy: Use the triangle inequality at each fixed positive separation, let both error probabilities vanish, and then pass through countably many separations.

items.title: Almost-sure convergence implies convergence in probability
items.strategy: Use measurable fixed-tolerance error indicators, which converge almost everywhere to zero and are dominated by one.

items.title: L^p convergence implies convergence in probability
items.strategy: Apply Markov's inequality to the p-th power of the difference at each fixed positive tolerance.

items.title: L^q convergence implies L^p convergence on a probability space
items.strategy: Specialize the finite-measure L^q-to-L^p inclusion to total mass one and apply it to each difference.

items.title: Convergence in probability implies convergence in distribution
items.strategy: At each continuity point, sandwich distribution functions using a positive tolerance and the probability of a large difference.

items.title: Convergence in distribution to a constant is convergence in probability
items.strategy: Use the continuity points c-epsilon and c+epsilon of the constant law to bound the probability of leaving its epsilon-neighborhood.

items.title: An almost-surely convergent subsequence from convergence in probability
items.strategy: Choose n_k as the least index larger than n_(k-1) with P(|X_nk-X|>2^-k)<2^-k; first Borel--Cantelli yields almost-sure convergence.

items.title: Subsequence characterization of convergence in probability
items.strategy: One direction uses almost-sure implies probability for every subsequence; the other extracts an almost-sure subsequence from any putative violating subsequence.

items.title: A metric for convergence in probability
Convergence in probability is metrized by d_0
items.strategy: Prove representative independence, symmetry, and the triangle inequality from min(1,a+b) <= min(1,a)+min(1,b), then show d_0=0 exactly for equality almost surely and compare E[min(1,|X-Y|)] with probability tails in both directions.

items.title: Dominated convergence in L^p
items.strategy: Apply dominated convergence to |X_n-X|^p, using the p-power domination supplied by a common L^p majorant.

items.title: Uniform integrability plus convergence in probability implies L^1 convergence
items.strategy: Identify probability convergence with convergence in measure for a probability measure and apply the finite-measure direction of the library's Vitali theorem to the sequence and limit.

items.title: L^1 convergence implies uniform integrability
items.strategy: Control late tails by the tail of the limit plus L^1 errors, and control the finitely many early terms separately.

items.title: Uniform integrability characterizes L^1 convergence under probability convergence
items.strategy: Combine the two preceding implications, with the family understood to include the proposed limit.

items.title: Slutsky's theorem for real random variables
items.strategy: Establish a tight real interval directly from distribution-function bounds, then use uniform continuity there. For quotients define X_n/Y_n arbitrarily on {Y_n=0}, and require the limiting c to be nonzero.

items.title: Complete convergence implication diagram
items.strategy: State the proved arrows and inline explicit witnesses for every failed converse and for failure of expectation convergence under almost-sure convergence.

items.title: Pairing preserves convergence in probability
items.strategy: For the product metric, bound a pair's error event by the union of the two coordinate error events.

items.title: Continuous maps preserve convergence in probability
items.strategy: Restrict to a compact interval or product rectangle carrying all but a small probability of the limit, use uniform continuity there, then bound the complement; include sums, products, and the nonzero-limit quotient convention.

title: Modes of Convergence for Random Variables — Examples

items.title: Convergence in probability need not be almost sure
items.strategy: On an independent product space take X_n=1_{E_n} with P(E_n)=1/(n+1). The probabilities vanish, while the divergent sum and second Borel--Cantelli give infinitely many spikes almost surely.

items.title: Almost-sure convergence need not imply L^p convergence
items.strategy: On (0,1), use nested shrinking spikes X_n=n^(1/p) 1_(0,1/n). They vanish pointwise away from zero but their L^p norms stay one.

items.title: L^p convergence need not imply almost-sure convergence
items.strategy: Use the dyadic typewriter sequence of indicators. Its interval lengths force every finite L^p norm to zero, while every non-dyadic point is hit and missed infinitely often.

items.title: Convergence in distribution need not be convergence in probability
items.strategy: For a symmetric two-point random variable X, take X_n=-X. The laws agree for every n, but |X_n-X| is bounded away from zero almost surely.

items.title: Convergence in probability need not imply L^p convergence
items.strategy: Use independent rare spikes X_n=n^(1/p)1_{E_n} with P(E_n)=1/n. Their probabilities of being nonzero vanish but every L^p norm equals one.

items.title: L^p convergence need not imply L^q convergence when p is less than q
items.strategy: On (0,1), take X_n=n^(1/q)1_(0,1/n). Its L^q norm stays one whereas its L^p norm tends to zero for p<q.

items.title: Almost-sure convergence does not imply convergence of expectations
items.strategy: The spikes X_n=n 1_(0,1/n) converge almost surely to zero but each has expectation one.

items.title: A probability-convergent sequence with a prescribed fast almost-sure subsequence
items.strategy: Make the least-admissible-index construction explicit for a selected summable tolerance schedule, showing how prescribed error thresholds produce an almost-sure subsequence.

items.title: Uniform integrability repairs the expectation limit
items.strategy: For a uniformly bounded sequence converging in probability, verify uniform integrability directly and invoke the L^1 characterization to obtain convergence of expectations.
